title: M268 cell 1: one big vs many small — generalist vs specialists on a shared held-out mix
registered_in: analysis/RESEARCH_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_v25.md (M268 registered 21 Aug; cell 1 dispatched 22 Aug, amendment 30)
question: On the same held-out mix read two ways, does routed per-representation specialization beat one generalist, and where does the routed arm's error come from (misroute vs correct-route arm error)?

generalist.role: one generalist serving every task type
generalist.decoding: greedy (do_sample=False), max_new_tokens 64, cudnn disabled (registered M267 env note)
generalist.anchor_note: no accuracy anchor claimed in cell 1; published card numbers are context; contamination declared

maths_primitive.engine: sympy exact integer arithmetic over a seeded generated expression tree
maths_primitive.anchor: determinism certificate — the truth values rebuilt from the seed and re-evaluated bit-exactly

logic_primitive.engine: deterministic boolean evaluator over a seeded generated expression tree
logic_primitive.anchor: determinism certificate — the truth values rebuilt from the seed and re-evaluated bit-exactly

sentiment_en.reuse_note: third configuration on this corpus — recorded re-use, product-quality boundary stands

arithmetic.note: integer arithmetic only (no division); intermediate and final values are exact integers; expression trees generated under the routing classifier's phrasing rules

boolean.note: literals are True/False constants; the final value is exact; trees generated under the routing classifier's phrasing rules

rules.sentiment: arm input begins with 'Classify the sentiment'

router.scope_note: the mix is generated under the classifier's rules, so cell 1 measures arm quality given perfect routing; natural-query / fingerprint-router routing is cell 2

grading.sentiment: generalist answer text (lowercased): LAST occurrence of 'positive'/'negative'; specialist label string mapped from id2label
grading.arithmetic: generalist answer text: LAST regex match of -?\d+ compared for exact integer equality with the exact tree value (echo-robust; raw answers recorded per item)
grading.boolean: generalist answer text (lowercased): LAST occurrence of 'true'/'false' (echo-robust; raw answers recorded per item)
